summary: Csaba Kiss is an Indologist who completed a D.Phil. at the University of Oxford (2003–2009) under Alexis Sanderson. He has held positions at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (attested 2021) and Eötvös Loránd University (attested 2026).

Specializing in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Sinology, Cuilan Liu served as Assistant Professor of Buddhist Studies at Emmanuel College, Toronto (attested 2017) and held an attested post at the University of Munich in 2018.

Culadasa (1944–2021) worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under traditional teacher Joti Dhamma Bhikkhu, served as director of the Dharma Treasure Buddhist Sangha (attested 2011), and taught Matthew Immergut.
Cuma Ozkan is a scholar in religious studies and Sinology who earned a Master of Arts at the University of Iowa under the supervision of Morten Schlütter (attested 2013).
Cunda studied under Ajahn Pasanno and Ajahn Amaro.

Cuong T. Mai is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He earned an MA at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa and a PhD at Indiana University Bloomington under John R. McRae, later becoming an Adjunct Lecturer at the University of Vermont.

Cynthea J. Bogel is a scholar in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. She completed her doctoral studies under John M. Rosenfield and held an attested post at the University of Washington from 2004 to 2009.
Cynthia Col studied Chinese religion at the Graduate Theological Union (attested 2003), working in the fields of Sinology and religious studies under teachers Mark Elliott and Steven D. Goodman.
Cynthia M. Beall (born 1949) studied at Pennsylvania State University (~1970–1976) and began her post at Case Western Reserve University in 1976, working in Tibetology and other fields.

Cynthia Talbot (born 1952) studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1981–1988). A specialist in history, archaeology, and Indology, she joined the University of Texas at Austin around 1995, where she is now Professor emeritus.

Cyril Henry Philips (1912–2005) studied at the University of Liverpool and SOAS. Working in history, archaeology, and Indology, he served as Director of SOAS from 1957 and as Vice-Chancellor of the University of London (1972–1976).

Cyrus Stearns is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned an MA under Turrell V. Wylie and a PhD from the University of Washington under Leonard van der Kuijp, also studying under traditional teachers and working as a translator for the Tsadra Foundation.
Cécile Ducher is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who completed her PhD at the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Matthew T. Kapstein, later serving as a research fellow there.

D. C. Lau (1921–2010) was a Sinology and philosophy scholar educated at the University of Hong Kong and University of Glasgow. He held posts at SOAS, the University of London, UCL, and The Chinese University of Hong Kong.
D. C. Sarasvati was an Indologist who studied under V. Raghavan and held an appointment as Lecturer-cum-Research Assistant at the University of Madras from 1964 to 1965.

D. Dennis Hudson (1938–2006) was a scholar of religious studies and Indology who taught in the Department of Religion and served as Professor in the Department of Religion and Biblical Studies at Smith College (~1970–2004).

D. L. Narasimhachar (1906–1971) was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied at Maharaja's College, Mysore (~1925–1929) and held a post at the University of Mysore from ~1932 to 1962, teaching T. V. Venkatachala Sastry.
Indologist D. N. Shukla earned a D.Litt. at the University of Lucknow under doctoral supervisor K. A. Subramania Iyer and held an attested post at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University in 1958.

D. Neil Schmid is a scholar in Sinology and Buddhist studies who studied at Waseda University, École Pratique des Hautes Études, and the University of Pennsylvania, completing his doctorate under Victor H. Mair.
D. R. Nagaraj (1954–1998) was an Indology scholar who studied at Bangalore University (~1973–1978) and subsequently held a post there (~1978–1998). He taught Sheldon Pollock.
